question: What is the lump-sum incentive for a Ph.D. for central government employees?
claude_answer: The lump-sum incentive for a Ph.D. or equivalent is **₹30,000**, per the **2022-09-16_higher-qualification-incentive** order. The **2021-08-13_ais-higher-qualification-incentive** order gives the same amount, but only for AIS officers.

question: How many times in a career can an employee receive the higher-qualification incentive and what is the minimum gap between grants?
reference_answer: Maximum two times with a minimum gap of two years
claude_answer: An employee can receive the incentive a maximum of two times in their career, with a minimum gap of two years between successive grants. Both the 2022-09-16_higher-qualification-incentive order (point 8) and the 2021-08-13_ais-higher-qualification-incentive order (point 5.8) state this.

question: Within what period must a government servant claim the higher-qualification incentive after acquiring the qualification?
claude_answer: A government servant should claim the incentive within six months of acquiring the higher qualification (2022-09-16_higher-qualification-incentive, para 9). The AIS order gives the same six-month limit for AIS officers, with a one-time exception for qualifications acquired on or after 01.07.2017 and before the order's issue date, which could be claimed within six months of that issue date (2021-08-13_ais-higher-qualification-incentive, para 5.10).

question: From which date are higher qualifications eligible for the incentive for All India Services officers?
claude_answer: Higher qualifications acquired on or after 01.07.2017 are eligible for the incentive for AIS officers, per 2021-08-13_ais-higher-qualification-incentive (para 5.9). The 2022-09-16_higher-qualification-incentive order also lists its rates as effective from 01.07.2017, but it covers government employees generally, not AIS officers specifically.

question: What is the incentive for a PG degree of more than one year for an IAS officer?
claude_answer: An IAS officer gets a one-time lump-sum incentive of **Rs 25,000** for a PG Degree/Diploma of more than one year, per **2021-08-13_ais-higher-qualification-incentive** (para 2, Sl. ii) and **2022-09-16_higher-qualification-incentive** (rates table, Sl. 2).

question: How long before the start of ex-India study leave should an application reach the cadre controlling authority?
claude_answer: Applications for ex-India study leave should be forwarded to the Cadre Controlling Authority at least 2 months before the study leave begins (ORDER: 2024-04-25_exindia-study-leave-consolidated). The order says "forwarded," not "received," so it does not state the exact arrival deadline.

question: What is the Central Deputation Reserve norm as a percentage of senior duty posts?
claude_answer: The Central Deputation Reserve norm is 40% of Senior Duty Posts (SDPs). This is stated in ORDER 2023-01-16_exindia-study-leave-rationalizing and ORDER 2024-04-25_exindia-study-leave-consolidated.

question: Can leave encashment be withheld for an AIS officer under suspension at retirement?
reference_answer: Yes the competent authority may withhold whole or part if money may become recoverable
claude_answer: Yes. The 2022-10-27_ais-leave-encashment-suspension order states that the authority competent to grant leave may withhold whole or part of leave encashment for an AIS officer under suspension or facing pending disciplinary/criminal proceedings at retirement, if some money may become recoverable, and the withheld amount is payable after adjustment of Government dues once proceedings conclude.

question: What is the maximum ex-India leave in conjunction with an official visit abroad for AIS officers?
reference_answer: 3 weeks and within 50 percent of the official duty period
claude_answer: The maximum is 3 weeks, subject to a limit of 50% of the official duty period abroad. For official visits shorter than 8 days, the 50% limit may be relaxed, allowing up to 4 days of ex-India leave. (2022-10-07_ais-exindia-leave-delegation)

question: Within what time must an LTC claim be submitted if no advance was drawn?
reference_answer: Within three months of the return journey
claude_answer: An LTC claim must be submitted within three months after the return journey if no advance was drawn (Rule 14, 2025-09-03_ltc-guidelines). The Ministry or Department may admit claims up to six months later, with Financial Advisor concurrence, without referring to DoP&T.

question: How many days of earned leave can be encashed when availing LTC?
claude_answer: Up to **10 days** of earned leave can be encashed at the time of availing LTC, for either type of LTC (home town or any place in India), under the 2025-09-03_ltc-guidelines order. Where a husband and wife are both Government servants, each may encash 10 days at the time of availing LTC, subject to a maximum of 60 days each during the career (same order).

question: How many days of Special Casual Leave can an organ donor get?
claude_answer: An organ donor can get a maximum of 42 days of Special Casual Leave, notwithstanding the usual 30-day limit in Appendix-III of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972. This is stated in ORDER: 2023-04-25_organ-donor-special-casual-leave and repeated in ORDER: 2025-04-08_leave-summary-oms.

question: What additional details must states submit with an ex-India study leave proposal for an IAS officer?
reference_answer: Central deputation details; officers on study leave vs leave reserve; officers returned in last two years with postings
claude_answer: States must submit (a) details of officers sponsored for Central Deputation in the previous and current year against the 40% CDR norm of Senior Duty Posts, (b) details of IAS officers on study leave within and outside India against Leave Reserve, and (c) details of officers who returned from study leave in the last two years and their postings. The 2024 order also requires the check-list it encloses to be provided. (2023-01-16_exindia-study-leave-rationalizing; 2024-04-25_exindia-study-leave-consolidated)

question: What is the limit on earned leave encashment for officers appointed on contract?
reference_answer: Not more than 10 days of earned leave encashment per completed year of service in the post; this replaces the earlier caps of 180/240/300 days; effective from 20 June 2019
claude_answer: Officers appointed on contract may encash earned leave at their credit on contract termination, up to 10 days for each completed year of service in that contract appointment. Days encashed in earlier government appointments are not counted. This replaces the earlier 300-day cap. (2019-06-20_leave-encashment-contract-officers; consistent with 2025-04-08_leave-summary-oms)
